text:
Priya: quick sync? thinking about feeding ML abuse scores into the edge rate limiter. want to capture design tradeoffs before i write an RFC :thinking:
Ian: +1. are we talking synchronous call per request or async enrichment + sidecar cache? latency budget matters here
Priya: target SLO at edge is 30ms P95 for auth+rate decisions. can't block on a 50ms model call. considering two modes: (A) fast local classifier at edge with periodic model updates, (B) async model call that updates tenant risk tokens used by admission
Zoe: for (A) we can quantize tiny models (TFLite/ONNX) and run in sidecar. cheap but risk of concept drift. need versioning + rollback hooks
Matt: also think about fairness: model scores might correlate with tenant size or workload. if we directly translate score -> quota, larger tenants could be unfairly favored/penalized
Sanjay: agree. propose we expose a simple interface from ML to admission: {score, confidence, model_version, reason_tags}. admission then applies tenant-normalization function and a guarded multiplier. keep logic in admission so rate service remains deterministic
Priya: example contract idea:
```json
POST /v1/abuse_score
{ "tenant_id": "T123", "request_id": "r-abc", "features": { /* optional */ } }
=> 200 { "score": 0.82, "confidence": 0.43, "model_version": "abuse-v4", "ttl_s": 300 }
```
Priya: note ttl to let edge cache expire stale signals
Ian: how do we handle adversarial clients who craft requests to poison scores? we need both input validation and monitoring for distribution shift
Zoe: pipeline idea: train with synthetic adversarial examples + monitor feature drift. also log hashed feature fingerprints (no PII) for auditing. + set conservative default when confidence low
Matt: rollout strategy: start with score-only telemetry in prod (no admission impact) -> shadow multiplier -> gradual canary ramp. A/B test across tenant buckets to measure throughput/latency/cost/regression on fairness metrics
Sanjay: telemetry needs to export per-tenant aggregated histograms: score distribution, actions taken, rejection rates, host latency. these feed the Optimize toolkit for recommendations
Priya: fallback: if ML service unavailable, admission should fall back to baseline policy (static heuristics) and mark decisions with "ml_unavailable" tag for postmortem
Ian: also need determinism for debugging: log model_version + seed + hashed inputs for requests that trigger rate changes (retain minimal amount)
Zoe: on infra: prefer an async fanout to regional model replicas with quorum read for high confidence, but allow single-replica read for low-latency soft decisions
Matt: one more: privacy. avoid sending raw user text to model. only send derived features or embeddings, and ensure KMS/HSM if any PII possible
ops-bot: deploybot: canary deployed abuse-v4 to eu-west1 (2/10 replicas) at 2026-03-23T15:12Z :rocket:
Priya: thanks. i'll draft RFC capturing: API contract, cache TTLs, admission normalizer hooks, rollout plan, telemetry schema, privacy guardrails. anyone want to add a short bullet before i post? :thumbsup:
Ian: add a sanity check endpoint for admission to fetch current multipliers per-tenant
Sanjay: include an offline simulation job to replay 7d of traffic and produce fairness/regression reports
Zoe: include model refresh cadence and a small-model training pipeline for edge variants
Matt: suggest we define a safety floor so model can't reduce quota below X% without human review
Priya: perfect, will send RFC draft in #eng-platform tomorrow morning
